content:
Recent public perception of Meta AI glasses has noticeably turned sour—so much so that among the top three spots on the US iPhone paid App Store chart today, one is occupied by an app specifically designed to detect who nearby is wearing smart glasses.

The app's name leaves nothing to the imagination: Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner, which claims to detect and alert you to anyone nearby wearing Meta AI glasses.

Enough iPhone users were willing to spend US$3 to try this app to propel it to third place on the US iPhone paid App Store chart—a remarkable achievement for a newly launched paid app.

We haven't tried the app ourselves, so we can't confirm whether it actually works; moreover, even if it does detect AI glasses, what you're supposed to do once you spot someone wearing them remains very much an open question.

Smart glasses equipped with cameras are still fairly easy to recognise in public these days, so you can probably spot who is wearing one without needing an app at all.

Still, the message from the public is unmistakable: a great many people are deeply uncomfortable with the very idea of AI smart glasses, viewing them as a privacy concern. If Apple intends to enter the smart glasses fray next year, this undoubtedly represents a significant headwind.
